I will keep to the wheat-maize rotation this year. In Quzhou County, that is the system I know best, it fits the climate and water conditions, and it is the safest way for me to keep output steady without taking on too much market or management risk. I am 61, so I do not want to spread myself across too many crops that need more labor, more sorting, or more complicated timing. I will use the same land for winter wheat first and then summer maize after harvest. For seed, I will use improved or hybrid varieties because I want stable emergence, stronger stress resistance, and more dependable yield than old saved seed. For fertilizer, I will put more nitrogen on maize and a balanced amount on wheat, with phosphorus and potassium kept at moderate levels because I need yield but I also need to control cost. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because it is practical for me and matches the machinery I would arrange locally. For irrigation, I will irrigate wheat more times because wheat in this area usually needs watering at key stages, while maize can often get by with less if summer rain is normal. I will still spray pesticides when needed, but I will keep applications limited to the main disease, weed, and insect pressure periods rather than spraying too many times. My whole plan is to stay with the familiar double-cropping system, control costs, reduce labor burden, and aim for a stable harvest over the full year.
